reconcile.connective: Commentators read "masters according to the flesh" as delegated bodily authority only — souls and exclusive worship remain God's alone.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible catalogues this exact pairing as contradictory: exclusive service to God alongside scripturally sanctioned obedience to human masters.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/serve.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: Civil servitude is not inconsistent with Christian liberty. Those may be the Lord's freemen who are slaves to men. "Your masters according to the flesh (Eph 6:5), that is, who have the command of your bodies, but not of your souls and consciences: God alone has dominion over these."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: MHC's block-anchored note on Eph 6:1-9 draws the exact reconciling distinction the row needs: human masters hold only delegated, bodily/civil authority, while souls and exclusive worship remain God's alone — directly answering the tension between Matt 4:10's 'him only shalt thou serve' and the household codes' command to obey human masters.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's "Ethical Discrepancies" chapter (p. 293) treats this exact pairing under the heading "Due to masters. / To God only," setting Col 3:22 and 1 Pet 2:18 against Matt 4:10 and Matt 23:8, and resolves it precisely as the row's reconcile pole does: "The first series refers to civil obedience, or obedience in secular matters; the last relates to worship and religious service."
